products.name: CrowdStrike Charlotte AI
products.note: Security operations AI; threat detection; autonomous response; high-privilege access

reading.body:
CrowdStrike, a public cybersecurity company, has positioned itself around the premise that AI systems require dedicated security infrastructure, offering threat detection and autonomous response through its Charlotte AI product.

The company frames its offering as a response to three shifts it sees as tied to the AI era: adversaries using AI to find and exploit vulnerabilities faster, breaches flowing through cloud infrastructure rather than traditional on-premises systems, and the need to secure AI models themselves. Charlotte AI sits within the Falcon platform, a cloud-native system that combines security data, automation, and AI intelligence to operate across endpoints, cloud workloads, identities, and data. This structure reflects a bet that security operations will be increasingly automated and that the perimeter of what needs defending has expanded from servers to models.

For AI scaling specifically, this matters because large compute infrastructure, whether in data centers or distributed cloud workloads, requires continuous security operations to remain viable. If threat detection and autonomous response at scale require purpose-built AI systems, then security becomes a load on the power and building infrastructure that AI itself demands. The data does not address whether Charlotte AI or the broader Falcon platform has measurable adoption among AI infrastructure providers, how much compute it consumes relative to what it protects, or whether it removes or adds to the net resource burden of maintaining AI systems.

profile_text.body:
CrowdStrike is a global cybersecurity company that describes itself as an AI-native cybersecurity leader. Its core offering is the Falcon platform, a cloud-native system designed to protect endpoints, cloud workloads, identities, and data by combining security data, AI intelligence, automation, and what the company calls elite expertise. The company also operates the CrowdStrike Cyber Superintelligence Lab, which brings together AI researchers, offensive operators, and incident responders. The lab's first announced development, SafeMind, pairs a component called Red Tempest for offense with Blue Solano for defense in a continuous learning loop intended to build cyber defenses that adapt to adversaries. Additional platform capabilities include unified agent and agentless cloud protection, AI model scanning, and an AI security dashboard.

CrowdStrike tracks one AI product on this site, Charlotte AI, which sits in the Security and Identity AI category and covers security operations, threat detection, autonomous response, and high-privilege access management. CrowdStrike is a publicly traded company listed on Nasdaq under the ticker CRWD, with SEC CIK number 0001535527. No litigation or MCP server registrations are currently held in this site's records for the company.
